actions.action: Remove fully crispy or brown leaves with clean scissors
Move the plant back from the window to bright, indirect light
Place it away from drafts, heaters and AC vents in a steady 18–27°C spot
Alternatively, raise humidity with a pebble tray
Alternatively, raise humidity by grouping plants together
Check the top few centimeters of soil and water thoroughly when dry
Check that the pot drains well and isn't sitting in water
Check whether the windowsill is drafty or cold at night
If damage spreads or the stem turns soft or black, check the roots

reason: The answer doubts cold damage and favors transport or humidity stress, mentioning cold only as a lesser possibility; it tells the owner to leave the stem alone and keep watering instead of cutting the plant back, withholding water and using a glass jar, which would delay the fix that worked.
